system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:58 UTC, WS-ICHEN-01 sent 51,000,389 bytes to the internal proxy at 10.40.20.30:8080 over a connection lasting about 9 seconds.

The available proxy records later show ivy.chen using Chrome to browse AWS pages and retrieve AWS static assets between 14:12 and 14:13 UTC; they do not identify the destination or purpose of the earlier large transfer.

Sysmon recorded svchost.exe accessing lsass.exe with GrantedAccess=0x1010 at 14:13:46 UTC. This warrants review, but the event alone does not establish that LSASS memory was read or credentials were extracted.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied record for the large transfer identifies the client, internal proxy endpoint, byte counts, and duration, but not the requested URL, HTTP method, external destination, or payload.
The supplied records do not include a matching proxy request or endpoint process attribution for the 13:45:58 transfer.
The later AWS browsing records occur after the large transfer and do not establish that the transfer was to AWS or related to that browsing.
claims_not_established: Whether the 51,000,389 bytes were forwarded beyond the proxy or what external destination received them.
Whether the transfer contained organizational data, and whether it was authorized.
Which process initiated the large transfer.
Whether the LSASS access event was benign service activity or credential-access activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve proxy access and TLS inspection logs for the 13:45:58 connection, including URL, method, authenticated user, destination, and upload or request-body byte counts.
Correlate the connection with endpoint process/network telemetry, including process creation, command lines, and file access around 13:45 UTC.
Review the source process and service configuration for the svchost.exe-to-LSASS access at 14:13:46, and check for corroborating credential-access or memory-dump evidence.
Confirm whether the transfer was expected with ivy.chen and the relevant business or IT owner.
